- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is trending up.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points) — cap forecast at 1–2 points below true peak.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in catching the reversal — adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5 points in next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >1.5σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 0.3–0.7 points; if below, raise by 0.2–0.5 points.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum — weight last 5–7 days more heavily in adjustment.
- If sentiment history shows 3+ consecutive 0.00 values, model underperforms — add 0.2–0.5 to forecast to counteract pessimism.
